title: Control-chart based drift detection + synthetic probe integration for embedding + reranker regressions
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Summary:
We need an automated detection and alerting pathway for gradual quality regressions to embedding + reranker pipelines that are tied specifically to config or model changes. The goal is earlier, lower-noise detection for small but sustained drops in offline recall/precision and to reduce human investigation time by surfacing root-candidate deltas (config field X, quantization profile, model-variant).

Motivation & scope:
- Existing regression signals are either too noisy (raw score drift) or too coarse (periodic snapshot evals).
- This ticket implements control-chart style monitoring (EWMA + CUSUM) on key metrics across cohorts and integrates synthetic probes that exercise known edge cases to increase sensitivity to regressions caused by config/model rollouts.
- Scope: offline post-deploy shadow evaluation, dashboarding, alerting rules, and an automated triage payload that attaches top-10 impacted probe examples and recent config deltas to alerts.

Design decisions (current):
- Metrics tracked: recall@k (k=1,5,10), precision@k, mean reciprocal rank (MRR), cosine-similarity distribution quantiles (p10/p50/p90), cohort perplexity proxy.
- Detection algorithms: EWMA for gradual shifts (alpha=0.2), CUSUM for persistent small shifts (h threshold tuned per-metric to target ~1% FPR), and a secondary KS-test on embedding distribution tails for sudden changes.
- Synthetic probes: a curated set of ~600 probe queries covering long-tail intents, paraphrase clusters, and adversarial paraphrases. Probes run in shadow for all config/model rollouts and are included in the alert payload.
- Attribution: when an alert fires, compute a config delta score by diffing rollout metadata (model, quantization, kernel flags, batching config) and ranking delta candidates by their association strength to metric drop (Spearman correlation on historical rollouts).

Acceptance criteria:
- Control-chart pipelines compute per-cohort time-series and can evaluate a 7-day rolling baseline for each metric.
- Alerts created in PagerDuty when EWMA or CUSUM crosses thresholds AND effect size on probe set >= 0.5% absolute drop for recall@5.
- Alert payload includes top-10 probe examples, last 5 config deltas, recent PR links, and a link to the per-model dashboard.
- Dashboards show control charts with annotated rollouts and an automated suggested rollback action (manual trigger).
- End-to-end test: simulate a synthetic regression by flipping a quantization flag in a staging rollout and verify an alert is created with correct payload and triage links.

Implementation plan & milestones:
1) Data plumbing (3d): sample embed + rerank offline metrics into a time-series store (Influx/Timescale) and add cohort keys. Owner: Aisha.
2) Detection service (4d): Python microservice that computes EWMA/CUSUM windows and emits alerts to events bus. Owner: Marco.
3) Probe harness (5d parallel): integrate synthetic probe runner into shadow-eval infra; store per-probe scores in same TS. Owner: S. Ramirez.
4) Dashboard + alerting rules (2d): Grafana panels and PagerDuty rules; include annotated rollout overlays. Owner: Observability team.
5) Rollout & canary (2d): enable for staging, validate with synthetic flip, then enable for production shadow only.

Progress updates:
- 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Observability and Product. Decided EWMA + CUSUM pair to balance sensitivity vs false positives.
- 2026-03-05: Probe set drafted (initial 600 probes) by S. Ramirez and PM. Shared probe taxonomy in Confluence.
- 2026-03-08: Data plumbing PR opened (https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1624). Basic timeseries ingestion validated on staging with one-week backfill.
- 2026-03-11: Detection service prototype computes EWMA on recall@5; tuning session tuned alpha and CUSUM h to target ~0.5% FPR on two months historical data.
- 2026-03-12: PagerDuty playbook drafted; includes links to rollback runbook for Dedicated customers.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Frequency vs cost: running full probe set on every small canary step increases cost. Proposed mitigation: run a compact probe subset (100 examples) for minor config diffs and full probe set for model changes or quantization updates.
- Sensitivity tuning: how to pick acceptable FPR across product tiers? Proposal: P0 customers use lower thresholds and P2/P3 use higher thresholds. Need PM decision.
- Attribution accuracy: correlation-based delta ranking is heuristic; long term we may need causal inference (A/B replay) to confirm.

Review feedback (from PM: Sophie Ramirez) on 2026-03-09:
- PM: "Strong direction; please ensure probe set has labeled expected outputs to compute precision-based deltas. Also add a per-customer opt-out for probe execution in Private deployments."
- Action: added probe labels and opt-out toggle requirement.

Testing & rollout notes:
- Staging test: flip quantization flag on model-variant vm-quant-08; run full probe set and validate alert payload (planned 2026-03-16).
- Canary policy: start with shadow-only for 1 week; if no high-severity alerts, enable alerting for infra on-call and P0 customer eng leads.

Follow-ups / future work:
- Auto-generate candidate mitigation steps (fallback to previous model, switch quantization profile) and present a 1-click rollback in console.
- Integrate with the regression evaluation harness to automatically open a PM ticket with artifact links when an alert persists >24h.
- Add cohort-aware dynamic thresholds that adapt to seasonality and traffic shifts.

Risks:
- False positives causing alert fatigue. Mitigation: dual-algorithm gating, minimum effect-size on probes, and burst-suppression window.
- Probe set maintenance overhead. Mitigation: quarterly review and semi-automated probe augmentation from real user failures.

Notes for oncall triage template (to include in PagerDuty):
- Short summary of the alert and top-3 likely config deltas
- Link to per-model control chart + recent PRs
- Top-10 probe examples with expected vs actual result
- Suggested immediate mitigations and rollback link
